> [!WARNING]
> **Pre-release — for personal testing only.** This build is meant for trying out the functionality yourself, not for rolling out to your clients. Stability is still poor, and updates will be frequent and breaking. If you need something dependable, wait for the `0.1.0` release.

Second ReClash pre-release. The same cross-platform proxy client built on the mihomo core, for Android, Windows, macOS and Linux. This build folds in a full config editor, a passive connection doctor, and a pile of hero, navigation and wallpaper polish on top of `pre.1`.

## What's new since pre.1

- Config editor: port the FlClash config editor with syntax highlighting.
- Connection doctor: surface VPN/TUN breaks passively on the home screen, and drill it into the Tools pane on desktop.
- Subscription hero: mark unlimited plans with ∞ time and traffic, hatch the bar, and size the desktop announcement tile to the orb column.
- Navigation: animate the proxies tab in and out, show a tooltip on the folded rail, and anchor tooltips to any edge.
- Global hotkeys now work on Wayland desktops.
- Core reports ReClashCore apart from the mihomo version in its passport.

## Fixes since pre.1

- Windows: drop the redundant UAC confirmation.
- Autostart: quote the exec path on Linux and Windows, repair stale entries, and park hidden windows.
- Wallpaper: stop the content flicker on toggle and crossfade it; keep the nav rail mounted across the frost toggle.
- Notifications now show the same active server the hero shows.
- Doctor holds the capture verdict unknown while the TUN listener warms up.
- Hero: repair the supernova gradient rendering and cut its graphics memory.

<!-- reclash:release-epoch:1 -->

## Notice

Out of the box this build identifies itself to subscription servers with the `FlClashX/v0.4.2` User-Agent, so existing provider panels keep serving clash configs. That header is the default preset, not the only option: you can pick another client identity in settings. Thanks to the [FlClashX](https://github.com/pluralplay/FlClashX) project, whose header ReClash borrows for compatibility until panels recognize its own identity.
